content: Root cause: The bug was caused by the assumption that all data packets would be of the ordinary data type, without accounting for the possibility of QoS (Quality of Service) data packets. Some access points (APs) were embedding EAP frames inside QoS data packets instead of ordinary data packets, leading to incorrect packet processing and potential failures in handling EAP frames. The patch adds support for recognizing QoS data packets, ensuring that the application can correctly process packets regardless of their type.

Code statements:
```c
-	return (
-                ((frame_header->fc &
-                        end_htole16(IEEE80211_FCTL_FTYPE | IEEE80211_FCTL_STYPE)) ==
-                        end_htole16(IEEE80211_FTYPE_DATA | IEEE80211_STYPE_DATA))
-		);
-	/* Is this a data packet ? */
-	if(!is_data_packet(frame_header))
-		return UNKNOWN;
```
